question: Why does ritual teaching present divisions of near and far if reality is partless?
premises: In this domain something shines forth by that will alone as far or near, according to the gradation of those who resort to it.
That reality remains untouched and established in a partless state.
Thus the division found in the section on ritual action appears in many ways.
inference: Ritual divisions reflect the gradation of practitioners, not a division in the partless reality itself.
plain_english: Here too something shines forth by that will alone as far or near, according to the gradation of those who take refuge; yet it remains untouched and established in the partless state. Thus the division belonging to the section on ritual action appears in many ways.
